manifest.name: dsh-pptx-builder
manifest.description: PowerPoint decks for DeepSeek Harness: pastel palettes, ten slide templates, styled text, web images, Python-rendered charts, highlighted code cards and LaTeX formulas (matrices, integrals, sums), plus a ready-made Presentations agent mode.
manifest.author: dsh-pptx-builder contributors

bundle.text:
# dsh-pptx-builder: one bundle with two Loader rows.
#
# 1. pptx-builder registers the Host tools (pptx_create, pptx_add_slide, ...).
# 2. preset-presentations adds the "Presentations" agent mode on top of them.
# The tools themselves stay visible in every mode; the preset only adds a
# purpose-built persona and a focused toolset.
- insert:
    - id: pptx-builder
      name: dsh-pptx-builder
      config: {}
    - id: preset-presentations
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset'
      config:
        id: presentations
        name: Presentations
        description: "Builds PowerPoint decks from reusable templates: pastel backgrounds, text slides, photos, Python charts, highlighted code and LaTeX formulas (matrices, integrals, sums)."
        order: 5
        plugins:
          - id: persona
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona'
            config:
              prefix: |-
                You are a presentation designer working in DeepSeek Harness. Your job is to turn the user's request into a polished Microsoft PowerPoint deck using the pptx_* tools.

                Workflow:
                - Work on a real .pptx file. If the user names one, follow it; when unsure whether it has editable state, call pptx_inspect first and continue with pptx_create only when there is no deck (ask before replacing a file that already exists).
                - Build every slide from a template instead of hand-placed boxes: pptx_add_slide with template "title", "section", "content", "split-left", "split-right", "chart", "code", "math", or "closing". Pass title, subtitle, text, presenter and image_url/image_path and the template places and centres everything.
                - Shape the narrative: title slide, section dividers, content and split slides, one chart per data idea, closing slide.
                - When the deck needs numbers from the outside world, search the web (web_search, web_fetch), take the figures and the source, and put them into pptx_add_chart. Never invent data; put the source in the chart's `source` field.
                - For a code slide, use template "code" and pptx_add_code: pass the snippet, the language, the file name in `title`, and highlight at most two or three key lines with `highlight_lines`. Keep lines under ~90 characters and the snippet under 60 lines, because the card scales as a whole.
                - For mathematics, use template "math" and pptx_add_math with LaTeX. Matrices: \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}; determinants: \begin{vmatrix} ... \end{vmatrix}; systems: \begin{cases} x, & x > 0 \\ -x, & x \le 0 \end{cases}; derivations: \begin{aligned} ... &= ... \\ &= ... \end{aligned}; calculus: \int_a^b, \sum_{k=1}^{n}, \prod, \lim_{x \to 0}, \frac{\partial f}{\partial x}, \nabla. Pass raw LaTeX without $, \[ \] or equation environments; 40-56 pt for the main result. Never write a formula as Unicode text in pptx_add_text, and never put a formula on a code or chart slide: it would be unreadable and unalignable.
                - To change something later, call pptx_inspect, find the element id, then pptx_update_element with only the fields that change.
                - When the user asks for an example, a starting point, or "what can you do", build one with pptx_gallery: style "features" tours every template, alignment, list style and chart kind, style "showcase" is a polished business deck. Present it, then reuse its slides and geometry as the visual reference for the deck at hand.
                - Finish by calling present with the .pptx path.

                Design rules:
                - The deck already has a pastel background from its palette (sand by default; mint, lavender, sky, rose are alternatives). Do not set a background per slide unless the user asks.
                - Geometry is in inches from the slide's top-left corner: 16:9 is 13.333 x 7.5, 4:3 is 10 x 7.5. Font sizes are points. The templates already handle centring, so do not override their geometry without a reason.
                - One idea per slide, at most six bullets, body text 16-20 pt, titles 28-36 pt.
                - Alignment and lists are the model's choice: `align` (left/center/right/justify) sets the body text, `title_align` the heading, and `bullet: true|false` switches between a bulleted list and one solid block. Long lists read best left-aligned; centred or right-aligned text suits short lines and single paragraphs. Vary it when the content calls for it, and use pptx_update_element to re-align an existing block instead of recreating the slide.
                - Use the palette keywords "ink", "muted", "accent" for any hand-placed text so it stays consistent with the theme.
                - Images need a direct PNG or JPEG link, not a web page; give each one alt text and leave room for a caption. Say where the picture came from.
                - Charts: on a "chart" template slide omit the chart-internal `title` (the slide has a heading), put units in `subtitle` or `y_label`, keep one chart per slide, and prefer the deck palette over custom colours.
                - Mathematics: one display formula per slide at 40-56 pt; a short statement belongs in the slide text, the formula goes below it. Split a long derivation into several slides instead of shrinking it below ~28 pt. Use \text{...} for words inside a formula, \mathbb{R} for number sets, \mathbf{v} for vectors, and \partial or \nabla for calculus. Never fake a formula with Unicode text in pptx_add_text (a lone symbol in a sentence is fine). An unknown command fails with its position, so fix the command rather than replacing the formula with plain text.
                - The .pptx is the deliverable: do not paste the whole deck into the chat. Summarize the structure and the path afterwards.
                - Answer in the user's language. If audience, length, or style would change the deck materially, ask one short question; otherwise pick sensible defaults and state them.
          - id: time-context
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-time-context'
          - id: tool-fs
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs'
            config:
              read: true
              readImage: true
              write: false
              edit: false
          - id: tool-web
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-web'
            config:
              fetch: true
              searchTimeoutMs: 60000
          - id: tool-ask-user
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-ask-user'
          - id: tool-todo
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-todo'
            config:
              allowParallelInProgress: true
          - id: present
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-present'
          - id: compaction
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              compaction: true
            config:
              - id: compaction-basic
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic'
              - id: command-compact
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-command-compact'

readme.text:
A plugin bundle that lets an agent build real Microsoft PowerPoint decks: pastel
palettes, ten reusable slide templates with exact geometric centering, styled
text boxes, internet images, charts rendered by Python, highlighted code cards,
and LaTeX formulas — matrices, integrals, sums with limits — typeset by the
plugin itself, with no LaTeX installation. It also ships a **Presentations**
agent mode tuned for deck work.

The `.pptx` package (ZIP + OOXML) is written by the plugin itself, so there is
no Office dependency, no network round-trip after an image is embedded, and the
file stays valid after every call.

Install the bundle into the current profile:

```text
plugin_manager { "action": "install_bundle", "target": "dsh-pptx-builder" }
```

Or use **Plugins → Install** in the Harness UI and paste the package name.
After a restart the tools show up in every mode, and a new **Presentations**
agent preset appears in the mode picker for a new session.

From a local checkout, pass the absolute directory instead of the package name.

The preset adds a persona that knows the workflow — inspect before editing,
build from templates, cite data sources, typeset mathematics with
`pptx_add_math`, finish with `present` — plus a focused toolset: the `pptx_*`
tools, file reading, web search/fetch, `present`, `todo_write`,
`ask_user_question`, and compaction. The tools themselves are registered
host-wide, so they are also usable outside this mode.

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `pptx_create` | Creates a deck on a pastel palette: size (`16:9` / `4:3`), palette, default font, accent, page-number placement. |
| `pptx_gallery` | Builds a ready-made reference deck: `features` tours every template, alignment, list style and chart kind; `showcase` is a polished business deck. |
| `pptx_add_slide` | Adds a slide from a template (`title`, `section`, `content`, `split-left`, `split-right`, `chart`, `code`, `closing`, `blank`) with a heading, text, presenter and photo. |
| `pptx_add_text` | Arbitrary text box: `role`, `x`/`y`/`w`/`h`, `font_size`/`font_face`/`bold`/`italic`/`underline`/`color`/`align`/`valign`/`bullet`. |
| `pptx_add_image` | Downloads an image by `url` (or reads a local `path`), embeds the bytes and places it; the aspect ratio is preserved. |
| `pptx_add_chart` | Renders a chart from data (bar, stacked bar, line, area, pie, donut) with Python and embeds it. |
| `pptx_add_code` | Renders a code snippet as a dark card with syntax highlighting, line numbers, a file-name header and highlighted lines. |
| `pptx_add_math` | Typesets a LaTeX formula — matrices, integrals, sums with limits, fractions, Greek letters —

Coordinates are inches from the top-left corner of the slide (16:9 is
13.333 × 7.5), font sizes are points, colours are `#RRGGBB`, a basic colour
name, or a palette keyword (`ink`, `muted`, `accent`, `background`).

| Template | Layout |
| --- | --- |
| `title` | Oversized centred heading, subtitle below, presenter line in the bottom-right corner. Page number off. |
| `section` | Divider: heading and subtitle centred on the slide. |
| `content` | Centred heading on top, a fixed-width text column underneath. |
| `split-right` | Photo fitted and centred in the right half; heading and text centred in the left half. |
| `split-left` | Mirrored: photo on the left, text on the right. |
| `chart` | Heading and caption on top, the lower two thirds reserved for `pptx_add_chart`. |
| `code` | Heading and subtitle on top, the rest reserved for `pptx_add_code`. |
| `math` | Heading and subtitle on top, an optional statement under them, the rest reserved for `pptx_add_math`. |
| `closing` | Large centred "Спасибо за внимание" (override with `title`), optional subtitle. |
| `blank` | Nothing but the background. |

Every template centres its content inside its own region: the photo in its half,
the heading and text in theirs, blocks centered vertically.

`pptx_create` takes `palette`: `sand` (default), `mint`, `lavender`, `sky`,
`rose`. A palette defines the pastel background of every slide, the body ink,
the muted secondary colour, the accent, and the chart series colours.

Alignment and text shape are parameters, not template defaults:

| Parameter | Values |
| --- | --- |
| `align` | `left`, `center`, `right`, `justify` for the `text` block |
| `title_align` | the same for the heading and subtitle |
| `bullet` | `true` for a bulleted list, `false` (default) for one solid block |

Defaults: `content` is left-aligned, `split-left` / `split-right` are centred
without bullets and left-aligned with them. Long lists read best on the left;
centred or right-aligned text suits short lines and single paragraphs. An
existing block can be re-aligned with `pptx_update_element` (`align`, `bullet`).

`pptx_add_chart` accepts data, not code:

```json
{ "file": "sales.pptx", "kind": "bar", "stacked": false,
  "categories": ["2021", "2022", "2023", "2024"],
  "series": [ { "name": "Revenue", "values": [10.2, 13.8, 17.1, 21.4] } ],
  "y_label": "bn RUB", "value_format": "auto",

Supported: `bar` (including `stacked`), `line`, `area`, `pie`, `donut`. The
renderer draws the palette background, a light grid, axis labels, a legend,
value labels and a source footnote. The image is 1800 × 1000 px and is embedded
into the deck.

Data pipeline: `web_search` / `web_fetch` find the numbers, the model puts them
into `categories` and `series`, `pptx_add_chart` draws the picture, and
`pptx_update_element` can move or resize it.

`pptx_add_code` renders a snippet into a dark rounded card — syntax
highlighting, line numbers, a file-name header, a language chip, and an accent
band on highlighted lines — and embeds it as a picture.

Languages: `python`, `javascript`, `typescript`, `json`, `bash`, `sql`, `text`.
Keep lines under ~90 characters and the snippet under 60 lines: the card scales
as a whole, so one long line shrinks all the code. The card is a picture — to
change the code, remove the element and add it again.

`pptx_add_math` typesets LaTeX into a transparent 300 dpi PNG and embeds it.
The formula is laid out by the plugin's own typesetter (`python/math.py`), so a
machine without TeX produces the same result, and the picture is placed at its
natural typographic size: a 44 pt formula is 44 pt tall on the slide.

| Construct | Syntax |
| --- | --- |
| Fractions, binomials | `\frac{a}{b}`, `\dfrac`, `\tfrac`, `\binom{n}{k}` |
| Roots | `\sqrt{x}`, `\sqrt[3]{x}` |
| Scripts | `x_i^2`, `\sum_{k=1}^{n}`, `\int_0^1`, `\lim_{x \to 0}` |
| Big operators | `\sum \prod \coprod \int \iint \iiint \oint \bigcup \bigcap \bigoplus` |
| Matrices | `matrix`, `pmatrix`, `bmatrix`, `Bmatrix`, `vmatrix`, `Vmatrix` |
| Systems, derivations | `cases`, `aligned` (`&` aligns, `\\` breaks a line), `array{cc}` |
| Delimiters | `\left( ... \right)`, `\left[ ... \right]`, `\left\{ ... \right.`, `\langle \rangle`, `\|x\|` |
| Greek | `\alpha` … `\omega`, `\Gamma` … `\Omega`, `\varepsilon`, `\varphi`, `\vartheta` |
| Letter styles | `\mathbb{R}`, `\mathcal{L}`, `\mathbf{v}`, `\boldsymbol{\alpha}`, `\mathrm{d}`, `\operatorname{rank}` |
| Accents | `\vec{a}`, `\hat{x}`, `\bar{x}`, `\tilde{x}`, `\dot{x}`, `\ddot{x}`, `\overline{AB}` |
| Symbols | `\partial \nabla \infty \pm \cdot \times \le \ge \ne \approx \equiv \in \notin \subset \subseteq \to \Rightarrow \Leftrightarrow \forall \exists` |
| Words | `\text{если } x > 0` |

The `math` template leaves the lower part of the slide free; `pptx_add_math`
places the formula there, centred, and shrinks it only if it would not fit.
`font_size` 40–56 pt suits a key result, 28–32 pt a secondary line. A
multi-line derivation stays in one call:

```json
{ "latex": "\\begin{aligned} (a+b)^2 &= a^2 + 2ab + b^2 \\\\ &= a^2 + b^2 + 2ab \\end{aligned}" }
```

An unsupported command fails with its position instead of producing a wrong
slide: `unsupported command \fraq at position 1`. Delimiters a model tends to
add (`$...$`, `\[...\]`, `\begin{equation}`) are stripped automatically.

`pptx_gallery` builds reference decks from code, so they always match the
current templates:

| `style` | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `features` | A tour: all ten templates, three alignments, list and solid text, both split slides, four chart kinds, two code cards, four formula slides, palettes and settings. |
| `showcase` | A polished ten-slide business deck: title, context, charts, photo slides, a metrics code card, closing. |

A `.pptx` cannot be edited incrementally without a model, so the plugin keeps
the deck document in `<name>.pptx.json` beside the presentation and rebuilds the
package from it on every change. The sidecar is the editable source; the `.pptx`
is always a valid output. Deleting the sidecar does not break the presentation,
but makes it not editable by the plugin.

Optional `config` fields on the `pptx-builder` Loader row:

| Field | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `font` | `Calibri` | Default text font. |
| `accent` | from the palette | Accent colour overriding the palette. |
| `maxImageBytes` | `20971520` | Size limit for a downloaded image (20 MB). |
| `pythonPath` | auto-detected | Python interpreter with Pillow for charts and code cards. |

- Charts and code cards are rendered by Python with Pillow. Harness ships such
  a runtime, and the plugin finds it automatically; on another setup point
  `pythonPath` at an interpreter where `import PIL` works.
- Images must be direct PNG, JPEG, GIF or BMP links. WebP and SVG are rejected
  with an actionable message, because PowerPoint cannot render them.

- Charts cover bar, stacked bar, line, area, pie and donut. No maps, heatmaps or
  3D charts.
- Formulas are high-resolution pictures, not editable PowerPoint equations: to
  change one, remove the element and add it again. The typesetter covers the
  subset above, not the whole LaTeX language — no equation numbering, `\tikz`,
  chemistry packages or custom macros.
- Photo templates fit the whole image (contain); there is no cropping.
- Animations, speaker notes, tables and native PowerPoint charts are not
  created.
- An image is downloaded when the tool runs; after that the deck is
  self-contained.
